Alex great conversation this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before a kickoff:

Recap:
- Goal: evaluate Redwood for product search augmentation (query rewriting + reranking) over a 4-week POC.
- Primary success metric: +15% CTR on recommended results and >90% relevance precision (top-3) on our curated test set.
- Secondary metrics: latency < 150ms p95, cost <= $X per 1k queries (TBD).

Proposed next steps:
1) You to confirm the business success criteria (CTR + relevance thresholds) and a point of contact for data access (samples + schema).
2) Redwood and Acme agree on an evaluation plan (offline rubric + online shadowing). I'm attaching a short rubric template to start.
3) Tech kickoff on Mon Jul 5
4) Define timeline & owner for weekly checkpoints; recommend weekly 30m syncs.

Can you confirm the success criteria and availability for a Jul 5 kickoff? We

Thanks,

Thanks Dylan for quick confirmations from our side:

- Confirmed success criteria: target +15% CTR on our recommended set; top-3 precision target 90% on the curated use-case queries. If we hit both, we consider the POC a success.
- Secondary: p95 latency target 150ms and cost targets TBD (we'll share budget range by EOD Fri).
- Data/contact: Priya Shah (cc) will own data delivery. She'll share sample logs + schema and a 1,000-query seed set for the offline eval.

Jul 5 kickoff is fine for our engineering lead (Liam); he can join the initial scoping.

One ask: please include both an "offline evaluation" rubric (scoring on curated set) and a short plan for "online shadow"/A/B shadowing so we can compare production behavior. Can you also outline how you'll grade borderline outputs (false positives vs safety/brand issues)?

-Alex
Head of Product, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC: evaluation plan & success criteria

Alex, thanks for the clarity. I pulled together a short evaluation plan and a proposed grading rubric (attached). Summary below and happy to iterate:

Evaluation approach (high-level)
- Week 0 (prep): data handoff, access, instrumentation, and kickoff; Redwood ingests 1k seed queries + schema.
- Week 1: offline eval on curated seed set using our rubric. Deliver baseline vs Redwood outputs and per-query scoring.
- Week 2-3: online shadow for a subset of production traffic (non-intrusive) to compare model outputs vs baseline and measure latency/ops impact.
- Week 4: wrap-up, final scoring, and decision readout.

Ownership
- Acme: Priya (data), Liam (eng lead), product stakeholders for sign-off.
- Redwood: Dylan (AE), Marissa (POC lead), Dev (engineering contact).

Grading rubric (summary; attached full sheet):
- Relevance (0-5): how well the suggestion answers intent (weight 40%)
- Precision top-3 (binary per query, aggregated) (weight 25%)
- Safety/brand compliance (0-4): policy violations or tone issues (weight 20%)
- Latency penalty: subtract points for p95 > 150ms (weight 10%)
- Operational friction (logs, errors) (weight 5%)

Scoring: normalized to 100 points; pass threshold = 75. We provide per-query CSV and a summary dashboard.

Attachments: acme_poc_eval_plan_v1.docx, acme_poc_scoring_rubric.xlsx

Next steps from our side: I set up the evaluation sheet and share the Drive link by EOD. Can Dev confirm integration steps for shadowing (endpoint + logging schema)?

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME POC: evaluation plan & success criteria

Hey all

TL;DR: we can do non-intrusive shadow for a 10% sample and export side-by-side responses + metadata to S3/Acme bucket.

Integration plan:
- We'll expose a readonly shadow endpoint that accepts the same request payload as production.
- For each shadowed request we'll log: request_id, timestamp, input_query, baseline_response_id, redwood_response, redwood_latency_ms, model_version, and a small sample of system logs. Logs serialized to newline-delimited JSON and pushed to the agreed S3 path.
- Data retention: we'll keep logs for 30 days unless you request a different retention window.
- Security: TLS + signed IAM role for write access; no PII to be stored other than query text (if you require redaction we can run a pre-ingest scrub).

Open questions for Acme:
- Where should we push the shadow logs (S3 bucket + prefix)?
- Are there any PII or compliance constraints we should apply to the seed queries?

I'll be on the Jul 5 kickoff to help wire this up.
